title: Intents
objectives: Pass data with extras and get results
Understand intent filters and pending intents

sections.markdown: An Intent is a messaging object used to request an action from a component — start an Activity/Service, deliver a broadcast, or ask another app to handle something (share, dial, open a URL).

rows: Any app that can handle it

sections.markdown: Implicit intents are matched against **intent filters** declared in other apps' manifests. A **PendingIntent** wraps an intent so another app/system (notifications, alarms) can run it later with your permissions.
Use the Activity Result APIs (registerForActivityResult) instead of the deprecated startActivityForResult for cleaner, type-safe results.

flashcards.back: Explicit names a specific component; implicit declares an action and lets any capable app handle it.
A manifest declaration saying which implicit intents a component can handle.
A token wrapping an intent so another app/system can execute it later with your app's identity.

quiz.q: To open a specific Activity in your app, use…
quiz.explain: Explicit intents name the exact target component.
The system matches the action/data against declared intent filters.

quiz.q: A notification action should use a…
quiz.explain: Notifications run later/in another process, so they need a PendingIntent.

challenges.text: Start a second activity and pass an extra; read it on the other side.
Use an implicit ACTION_SEND intent to share text/an image.
Declare an intent filter so your app appears in the share sheet for a custom type.

interviewQuestions: What is a PendingIntent and when is it needed?
